learn.hook: Your mother checks the sky before hanging clothes out to dry. She is reading the weather!
points: Weather is the condition of the air (atmosphere) at a particular place and time. It can change within hours or days.
The main elements of weather are temperature, air pressure, humidity, wind (speed and direction) and precipitation (rain, snow or hail).
Temperature tells how hot or cold the air is. Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air; on a humid day sweat dries slowly and we feel sticky.
Air pressure is the weight of the air pressing down on us. It is lower at higher altitudes, like on mountains.
Wind is moving air. It blows from areas of high pressure towards areas of low pressure.

example.q: On a hot afternoon in Chennai, wet clothes take longer to dry than on a hot afternoon in Jaipur. Why?
steps: Chennai is on the coast, so its air holds a lot of water vapour: humidity is high.
Jaipur is far from the sea and its air is dry: humidity is low.
Water evaporates from clothes slowly when the air is already full of moisture.
example.answer: Because the humidity in Chennai is higher, so evaporation is slower.

learn.reallife: Before a cricket match, commentators talk about humidity, wind and the chance of rain because these affect how the ball moves and whether play can continue.

Humidity

games.title: What does it describe?
pairs: How hot or cold the air is

quiz.q: Weather means the condition of the atmosphere:
options: At a place over a short time
quiz.explain: Weather is about the air at a place now or over a few hours or days. The long-term average is climate.
steps: Weather is the condition of the air at a place and time.
It can change within hours or days.
The average over 30 years or more is climate, not weather.
Answer: At a place over a short time
quiz.mistake: Confuses weather with climate

quiz.q: The amount of water vapour in the air is called:
quiz.explain: Humidity measures moisture in the air. High humidity makes us feel sticky.
steps: Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air.
Air pressure is the weight of air; temperature is how hot or cold.
So the answer is humidity.
Answer: Humidity
quiz.mistake: Mixes up humidity with temperature

quiz.q: Wind blows from:
options: Low pressure areas to high pressure areas
High pressure areas to low pressure areas
Only from the sea to the land
quiz.explain: Air moves from where pressure is higher to where it is lower, just like air rushing out of a pumped-up balloon.
steps: Wind is moving air.
Air moves from where pressure is higher to where it is lower.
So wind blows from high pressure areas to low pressure areas.
Answer: High pressure areas to low pressure areas
quiz.mistake: Reverses the direction of air movement

quiz.q: What happens to air pressure as you climb a high mountain?
options: It becomes zero at the foot of the hill
quiz.explain: There is less air above you at greater heights, so the air pressure is lower.
steps: Air pressure is the weight of air pressing down.
Higher up, there is less air above you.
So the pressure decreases as you climb.
Answer: It decreases
quiz.mistake: Thinks being higher means more air pressing down

quiz.q: Which of these is a form of precipitation?
quiz.explain: Precipitation is water falling from clouds: rain, snow, sleet or hail. Dew and fog form near the ground and do not fall from clouds.
steps: Precipitation is water falling from clouds: rain, snow, sleet or hail.
Dew and fog form near the ground; smoke is not water.
So hail is precipitation.
Answer: Hail
quiz.mistake: Thinks any water drop in the air is precipitation

quiz.q: On a very humid day, why do we feel sticky?
options: The air has no water vapour
quiz.explain: When the air is full of moisture, sweat evaporates slowly, so it stays on our skin.
steps: On a humid day the air is already full of moisture.
Sweat then evaporates slowly and stays on our skin.
So we feel sticky because sweat does not evaporate quickly.
Answer: Sweat does not evaporate quickly
quiz.mistake: Does not link humidity with evaporation

quiz.q: Which pair are both elements of weather?
quiz.explain: Temperature and wind describe the state of the air. The others are features of the land.
steps: Elements of weather describe the air: temperature, pressure, humidity, wind, precipitation.
Soil, rocks, rivers, mountains, forests and deserts are land features.
So temperature and wind.
Answer: Temperature and wind
quiz.mistake: Mixes up landforms with weather

quiz.q: Which statement describes weather, not climate?
options: Kerala gets heavy rain every monsoon
Rajasthan is dry most of the year
It is raining heavily in Kolkata this evening
quiz.explain: 'This evening' is a short time at one place: that is weather. The others are long-term patterns, which is climate.
steps: Weather is a short time at one place; climate is a long-term pattern.
'This evening' in Kolkata is a short time.
The other statements describe every monsoon or most of the year, which is climate.
Answer: It is raining heavily in Kolkata this evening
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the time span in the statement

teach.ask: Gappu's feathers got wet in the rain. He asks: what is weather made of?
teach.praise: Temperature, humidity, pressure, wind and rain together make the weather. Now I know what to check before flying!
teach.nudge: You told me some parts. What about the moisture in the air, or the moving air?

revise.summary: Weather is the condition of the air at a place and time, and it can change within hours. Its elements are temperature, air pressure, humidity, wind and precipitation.
focus: Name and explain the elements of weather
Explain how humidity affects drying and sweating
Know how air pressure changes with height and how wind blows
remember: Elements: temperature, air pressure, humidity, wind, precipitation
Humidity = water vapour in the air
Air pressure is lower at higher altitudes
Wind blows from high pressure to low pressure
traps: Don't mix up weather (short-term) with climate (the long-term average)
Dew and fog are not precipitation
Wind does not blow from low to high pressure

learn.hook: A weather station is like a doctor's kit for the sky: each instrument checks one sign of the weather's health.
points: A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius (°C). A maximum-minimum thermometer records the highest and lowest temperature of the day.
A barometer measures air pressure. A falling barometer reading often warns of stormy or rainy weather.
A hygrometer measures humidity. A rain gauge measures rainfall, usually in millimetres (mm).
A wind vane shows the direction the wind is coming from; an anemometer, with spinning cups, measures wind speed.
Instruments are kept in an open space; thermometers are kept in a shaded, airy white box called a Stevenson screen so sunlight does not heat them directly.

example.q: Neha's school rain gauge collected 12 mm on Monday, 30 mm on Tuesday and 18 mm on Wednesday. What was the total rainfall?
steps: Add the three readings: 12 + 30 + 18.

learn.reallife: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), set up in 1875, runs weather stations across India and gives the forecasts you see on the news.

items.q: Rain on Mon 10 mm, Tue 15 mm. Total in mm?
Rain 20 mm a day for 3 days. Total mm?

quiz.q: Which instrument measures air pressure?
quiz.explain: A barometer measures the pressure of the air.
steps: A barometer measures air pressure.
A thermometer measures temperature, an anemometer wind speed, a rain gauge rainfall.
So the barometer.
Answer: Barometer
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of weather instruments

quiz.q: An anemometer is used to measure:
quiz.explain: The anemometer's cups spin faster in stronger wind, measuring speed. Direction is shown by a wind vane.
steps: An anemometer has cups that spin faster in stronger wind.
So it measures wind speed.
Wind direction is shown by a wind vane.
Answer: Wind speed
quiz.mistake: Confuses wind speed with wind direction

quiz.q: Rainfall is usually measured in:
quiz.explain: A rain gauge shows the depth of rain collected, measured in millimetres.
steps: A rain gauge collects rain and shows its depth.
Depth is measured in millimetres (mm).
Kilograms and °C measure weight and temperature.
Answer: Millimetres
quiz.mistake: Uses a unit of weight or temperature for rainfall

quiz.q: Why are thermometers at a weather station kept inside a shaded, airy box?
options: To keep them away from children only
So they can measure rainfall too
Because thermometers need darkness to work
So direct sunlight does not heat them and give a wrong reading
quiz.explain: We want the temperature of the air, not of a thermometer heated by sunshine, so it is kept in the shade with air flowing through.
steps: We want the temperature of the air.
Sunlight falling on a thermometer would heat it and give a wrong reading.
So it is kept in a shaded, airy box (a Stevenson screen).
Answer: So direct sunlight does not heat them and give a wrong reading
quiz.mistake: Does not realise sunlight on the instrument changes the reading

quiz.q: A town's highest temperature today was 36 °C and the lowest was 24 °C. What was the difference in °C?
quiz.explain: Difference = 36 − 24 = 12 °C.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two readings instead of subtracting
steps: Answer: 12

quiz.q: A school recorded rain: Mon 8 mm, Tue 20 mm, Wed 0 mm, Thu 12 mm. What was the total?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one of the days while adding
steps: Answer: 40 mm

items: Mon
Tue
Wed

quiz.q: Which organisation gives official weather forecasts for India?
quiz.explain: The IMD is India's national weather service and issues forecasts and warnings.
steps: India's national weather service issues official forecasts and warnings.
That is the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
ISRO launches satellites but does not issue the forecasts.
Answer: India Meteorological Department
quiz.mistake: Thinks the space agency issues the forecasts because it launches weather satellites

quiz.q: A hygrometer tells you:
options: How much moisture is in the air
quiz.explain: A hygrometer measures humidity, the water vapour in the air.
steps: A hygrometer measures humidity.
Humidity is the moisture (water vapour) in the air.
So it tells how much moisture is in the air.
Answer: How much moisture is in the air
quiz.mistake: Mixes up humidity with rainfall

teach.ask: Gappu wants to build a weather station in his tree. Which instruments does he need, and what does each measure?
teach.praise: A thermometer, barometer, rain gauge and wind instruments. My tree is now a science lab!
teach.nudge: Good! But how will I measure the rain, or which way the wind blows?

revise.summary: Weather is measured with instruments: a thermometer for temperature, a barometer for air pressure, a hygrometer for humidity, a rain gauge for rainfall in mm, and a wind vane and anemometer for wind direction and speed.
focus: Match each weather element to its instrument
Know the units used, like °C and mm
Explain why thermometers are kept in a shaded, airy box
Work with simple readings like totals and differences
remember: Stevenson screen: shaded, airy white box for thermometers
traps: An anemometer measures speed, not direction
Rainfall is measured in millimetres, not kilograms
Don't keep a thermometer in direct sunlight; it gives a wrong reading

topics.title: Weather forecasts and why they matter

learn.hook: Fishermen in Odisha stay ashore when a cyclone warning comes. A good forecast can keep whole villages safe.
points: A weather forecast is a scientific prediction of the weather for the coming hours or days.
Forecasters use readings from weather stations, weather balloons, radars and satellites, and powerful computers to make predictions.
Farmers use forecasts to decide when to sow, water and harvest. Pilots, sailors and fishermen check forecasts before setting out.
Early warnings of cyclones, heavy rain and heatwaves help people prepare and move to safety in time.
Weather changes from day to day, but the average pattern of weather over many years (usually 30 years or more) is called climate.

example.q: The forecast says heavy rain will fall tomorrow in a village. What should a farmer who planned to spray fertiliser on his field do?
steps: Heavy rain can wash fertiliser off the field.
That would waste money and the fertiliser could flow into ponds and streams.
So it is wiser to wait until the rain has passed.
example.answer: Postpone spraying until after the rain.

learn.reallife: Your family's phone weather app and the evening news both use data from the IMD and its satellites.

games.title: How a forecast is made
items: Instruments and satellites record weather data
Data is sent to the weather centre
Computers and experts study the data
A forecast or warning is announced to the public

games.title: Weather or climate?
items: A forecast tells us what the weather is likely to be in the coming days.
Forecasts are predictions for the near future.
Climate is the weather of a single afternoon.
Climate is the average weather pattern over many years.
Satellites help forecasters watch clouds and cyclones from space.
Weather satellites send pictures of clouds and storms.
Weather forecasts are of no use to farmers.
Farmers plan sowing, watering and harvesting using forecasts.
Early cyclone warnings help people move to safe shelters.
Warnings give time to prepare and evacuate.

quiz.q: What is a weather forecast?
options: A scientific prediction of coming weather
A record of last year's weather
quiz.explain: Forecasts use measurements and science to predict what the weather is likely to be.
steps: Forecasters use measurements from stations, balloons, radars and satellites.
They use science and computers to predict coming weather.
So a forecast is a scientific prediction of coming weather.
Answer: A scientific prediction of coming weather
quiz.mistake: Thinks forecasts are random guesses

quiz.q: Which tool lets forecasters watch a cyclone forming far out at sea?
quiz.explain: Satellites in space photograph clouds and storms over the ocean.
steps: A cyclone far out at sea cannot be seen by ground instruments.
Weather satellites in space photograph clouds and storms over the ocean.
So a weather satellite.
Answer: Weather satellite
quiz.mistake: Thinks ground instruments can see storms far away

quiz.q: Climate is best described as:
options: The average weather of a place over many years
The amount of rain in one day
quiz.explain: Climate is the long-term pattern, usually averaged over 30 years or more.
steps: Weather changes day to day.
Climate is the average pattern of weather over many years (usually 30 or more).
So climate is the average weather of a place over many years.
Answer: The average weather of a place over many years
quiz.mistake: Confuses climate with weather

quiz.q: Why is an early cyclone warning useful for coastal villages?
options: People get time to move to safe places and secure boats
quiz.explain: A warning cannot stop a cyclone, but it gives time to prepare and stay safe.
steps: A warning cannot stop or change a cyclone.
It gives people time to prepare.
So they can move to safe places and secure boats.
Answer: People get time to move to safe places and secure boats
quiz.mistake: Thinks a forecast can control the weather

quiz.q: A farmer hears that rain is expected in two days. How can this help her?
options: She can plan sowing so seeds get the rainwater
She must harvest all crops today
She should stop farming for the year
It has no effect on farming
quiz.explain: Sowing just before rain helps seeds get water naturally.
steps: Seeds need water after sowing.
If rain is coming in two days, sowing just before it gives seeds rainwater naturally.
So she can plan sowing so seeds get the rainwater.
Answer: She can plan sowing so seeds get the rainwater
quiz.mistake: Does not see how forecasts guide farm work

quiz.q: Which of these people most needs a wind and sea forecast before work?
options: A fisherman going out to sea
quiz.explain: Strong winds and rough seas are dangerous for small fishing boats.
steps: Strong winds and rough seas are dangerous for small boats.
A fisherman going out to sea faces this danger.
So he most needs a wind and sea forecast.
Answer: A fisherman going out to sea
quiz.mistake: Does not link weather with safety at sea

quiz.q: In which year was the India Meteorological Department set up?
quiz.explain: The IMD was established in 1875.
steps: The India Meteorological Department is India's national weather service.
It was set up in 1875, long before Independence.
So the year is 1875.
Answer: 1875
quiz.mistake: Assumes it was set up after Independence

quiz.q: Which statement is about climate?
options: It is cloudy in Pune this morning
A storm hit Puri last night
It is 30 °C in Bhopal right now
Mawsynram gets very heavy rain year after year
quiz.explain: A pattern repeated year after year is climate. The others describe a single time.
steps: Climate is a pattern repeated year after year.
'Mawsynram gets very heavy rain year after year' is such a pattern.
The others describe one morning, one night or right now: weather.
Answer: Mawsynram gets very heavy rain year after year
quiz.mistake: Does not notice whether the statement is long-term or short-term

teach.ask: Gappu doesn't understand why the TV shows a weather map every evening. Explain what a forecast is and how it helps.
teach.praise: So forecasts use data to warn and help people. I'll check one before my next long flight!
teach.nudge: You explained what a forecast is. But who uses it, and how does it keep people safe?

revise.summary: A weather forecast is a scientific prediction made from station readings, balloons, radars, satellites and computers. Forecasts help farmers, pilots, sailors and fishermen, and early warnings save lives; climate is the long-term average of weather.
focus: Explain what a forecast is and how it is made
Explain how forecasts help farmers and people at sea
Explain why early cyclone warnings matter
Tell statements about weather from statements about climate
remember: Forecast = scientific prediction of coming weather
Tools: weather stations, balloons, radars, satellites, computers
Climate = average weather over many years (usually 30+)
India Meteorological Department (IMD), set up in 1875
traps: A warning cannot stop a cyclone; it gives time to prepare
Don't call one day's rain climate; it is weather
